Thanks Ava — this is helpful. Appreciate the clear ask and the timing notes. Below are three pragmatic options we can surface to procurement; I tried to balance LuminaGrid's PO timing needs with guardrails that protect our unit economics during a fast ramp:

Option A — Price-hold + tiered uplift (recommended)
- 12-month price hold on current baseline rate for existing committed usage
- Incremental capacity priced at step discounts: +1.5x = -4% (off list), +2x = -6%, +3.5x = -9%
- First 60 days of incremental usage covered by a one-time ramp credit equal to 10% of estimated incremental spend (applied to next invoice)
- Monthly invoicing; overage billed at published overage rates after tier thresholds

Option B — Short-term bridge + quarterly invoicing
- 6-month price hold for baseline only
- 3-month bridge credit to absorb early ramp spikes (fixed credit: $25k)
- Quarterly invoicing to align with procurement POs

Option C — Commitment ladder with invoice smoothing
- Multi-step commit: Tiered minimums for 3, 6, 12 months with stepped discounts as in Option A
- Invoicing smoothed monthly with the ability to net invoices against bridge credit in month 1-2

Operational notes / asks from our side:
- Need a firm signal on expected uplift cadence (rough monthly ramp numbers) to size the bridge credit accurately
- Prefer DocuSign amendment for the price-hold + ramp-credit so we can preserve existing master terms
- Will propose a capped overage protection for the first 90 days if LuminaGrid can agree to a 6-month minimum on expanded capacity

I'm attaching a draft amendment (Draft_Amendment_v2.docx) that models Option A and includes the PO phasing language. Can you confirm which option procurement prefers and whether monthly invoicing is a hard constraint? Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow 10am PST if that's useful.

Best,

David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
